title: Everyday idioms
about: a piece of cake, once in a blue moon, pull somebody’s leg

entries.ex: The exam was a piece of cake.
He told a joke to break the ice.

entries.en: cost an arm and a leg
entries.ex: This bag cost an arm and a leg.
I’m exhausted — I’m going to hit the sack.
I’m feeling a bit under the weather today.

entries.ru: очень редко, раз в сто лет
entries.ex: We go to the theatre once in a blue moon.
When he forgot my birthday, that was the last straw.
Who spilled the beans about the party?

entries.en: let the cat out of the bag
entries.ex: I wanted to surprise her, but my brother let the cat out of the bag.

entries.en: hit the nail on the head
entries.ex: You’ve hit the nail on the head — that’s exactly the problem.
We’ve done enough — let’s call it a day.
Don’t cut corners when it comes to safety.
He got cold feet the day before the wedding.
He’s in hot water with his boss again.
Can you keep an eye on my bag?

entries.ru: на одной волне, понимать друг друга одинаково
entries.ex: Let’s make sure we’re all on the same page.
Don’t worry, I’m just pulling your leg.
My dad and I don’t see eye to eye on politics.
You can’t sit on the fence for ever — decide!

entries.en: the ball is in your court
entries.ex: I’ve made my offer. The ball is in your court now.
Stop beating around the bush and tell me!
Losing that job was a blessing in disguise.
You finally called! Better late than never.

entries.en: bite off more than you can chew
entries.ex: I bit off more than I could chew with three jobs.

entries.en: by the skin of your teeth
entries.ex: We caught the train by the skin of our teeth.

entries.ru: плакать о том, чего не вернёшь
entries.ex: It’s done — no use crying over spilt milk.

entries.en: every cloud has a silver lining
entries.ex: Every cloud has a silver lining.
The party got a bit out of hand.
She always goes the extra mile for her clients.
Hang in there — it’ll get easier.

entries.ru: это не бином Ньютона, не так уж сложно
entries.ex: Come on, it’s not rocket science!

entries.en: kill two birds with one stone
entries.ex: I’ll visit Mum and pick up the parcel — kill two birds with one stone.
It’s hard to make ends meet on one salary.
Tickets sold out in an hour — we missed the boat.

entries.ru: без труда не выловишь и рыбку из пруда
entries.ex: Training is hard, but no pain, no gain.
You’re on thin ice — one more mistake and you’re out.

entries.ru: как гром среди ясного неба, внезапно
entries.ex: He called me out of the blue after ten years.
We don’t have a plan — let’s play it by ear.
Pull yourself together — people are watching.
It’s raining cats and dogs out there!

Working from home gives me the best of both worlds.

entries.ru: в горе и в радости, несмотря ни на что
entries.ex: They’ve stayed together through thick and thin.
Time flies when you’re having fun.
Our holiday plans are still up in the air.
He’ll clean his room when pigs fly.
“It’s hot today.” — “You can say that again!”
Our donation is just a drop in the ocean.

entries.ru: судят по делам, а не по словам
entries.ex: Don’t promise — actions speak louder than words.

entries.en: don’t judge a book by its cover
entries.ex: The café looks awful, but don’t judge a book by its cover.
Driving is hard at first, but you’ll get the hang of it.

entries.en: have a lot on your plate
entries.ex: I can’t help — I’ve got a lot on my plate right now.
Keep your fingers crossed for my interview!
It took me a month to learn the ropes at the new job.
She was over the moon about the news.
These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg.
Don’t throw in the towel yet!
